content_preview.title: Swedish Court Orders Google to Pay Record Damages to Klarna's PriceRunner Over Shopping Search Bias
content_preview.summary: Stockholm's Patent and Market Court found Google unlawfully favored its own price comparison service, awarding PriceRunner what a judge called the largest damages in a Swedish competition case.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Stockholm's Patent and Market Court has ordered Alphabet's Google to pay 14.3 billion Swedish kronor plus interest in damages to PriceRunner, the price comparison service owned by payments company Klarna, for favoring its own shopping service in search results. The judgment was delivered on July 1, 2026, according to [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/business/2026/07/01/google-ordered-to-pay-klarnas-pricerunner-13-billion-over-search-abuse), which reported the award as roughly €1....

editor_notes.content_quality: Tightly written 519-word News piece with a clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. Attribution is scrupulous — every specific is inline-cited to the outlet that supports it, and the two reported currency figures (€1.7bn from Euronews, $1.46bn AFP base figure from Tech Xplore) are correctly separated rather than conflated.
editor_notes.source_verification: 3 sources. source-0.html.gz (Euronews, HTTP 200) — CONFIRMS: 14.3bn SEK plus interest / €1.7bn award, PriceRunner owned by Klarna, claim filed in Stockholm in 2022, ~80bn SEK sought with majority dismissed, Patent and Market Court, 'unlawfully favoured' finding, 2017 EC €2.42bn fine, decision upheld by EU's highest court in 2024, and the Mathilde Méchin quote ('We [Google] don't agree with the court's decision, we are reviewing and will consider our legal options' — article trims the '[Google]' bracket, substance verbatim). source-2.html.gz (European Commission newsroom, HTTP 200) — CONFIRMS: €2.42bn fine and the exact quote 'Google has abused its market dominance as a search engine by giving an illegal advantage to another Google product, its comparison shopping service,' plus the decision date 27/06/2017 matching the article's '27 June 2017.' source-1 (Tech Xplore/AFP) — snapshot FAILED with HTTP 403 (bot-blocked, file: null in manifest). Per policy I fell back to a live WebFetch of the URL, which CONFIRMED verbatim: the $1.46bn base figure, the full Judge Linda Kullberg quote ('In many ways, this is a complex and wide-ranging case, and although Pricerunner has not been entirely successful in its claim, the damages awarded are undoubtedly the largest ever ordered in a Swedish competition case.'), the core-finding quote ('Pricerunner is deemed to have suffered damage as a result of Google having, for many years, unlawfully favored its own price comparison service.'), and the time-barred/'brought too late' portion of the claim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, dates, party names, court name, judge name, and every direct quote trace to a cited source and were confirmed verbatim. The link from the 2017 EU Google Shopping fine to this private follow-on damages claim is accurately drawn and correctly framed as the regulatory foundation. No hallucinations detected.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The ruling is explicitly presented as contested — Google's disagreement and its 'reviewing and will consider our legal options' posture are quoted, the 'What We Don't Know' section flags that no formal appeal is yet confirmed and that survival of the award on review is open, and the Analysis avoids editorializing about the outcome.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Prior coverage of the June 2026 EU DMA fine against Google (2026-06/02) is a separate prospective regulatory action and does not mention PriceRunner; the March 2026 BNPL article mentions Klarna only in passing. No duplication.
concerns: Tech Xplore snapshot could not be archived (HTTP 403 bot-block), so its claims are not preserved in the provenance snapshot set. I verified those claims verbatim via live WebFetch; the Euronews and EC snapshots independently corroborate the central award figure, the 'unlawful favouring' finding, and the 2017 EC fine, so no load-bearing claim rests on the unarchived source alone.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: APPROVE.
